rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every pronoun/demonstrative resolves within its own chunk or against the chunk's own header (in-chunk by the rule's own carve-out): chunk 1 L25 "It can also stop short" -> Claude, named same sentence; chunk 4 L47/L49 "how full it is"/"what fills it" -> the context window, named same chunk; chunk 5 L57 "whether it is the right load" -> the load, same chunk. The one cross-header naming swap, chunk 5 L58 "The slice Claude didn't load" under header "The slice the agent didn't load" (L55), is the accept-noted swap at L66 (Antti 2026-09-10) — not a referent failure, a deliberate synonym. Harm this rule guards (a referent the reader can't place) is absent throughout.

No "the opening lecture said"-shaped callback anywhere in body. Closest candidate is the one external pointer, chunk 4 L53 "Use [ccstatusline](https://github.com/sirmalloc/ccstatusline)" — named, not located by page position, so it clears under the navigational-pointer carve-out even though it isn't a cross-doc curriculum link. Arc pointers ("Picks up from: Connections...") live in the maintainer block below the cut, out of slide scope.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Every chunk carries a self-standing claim or instruction. Closest candidate to an orphan is chunk 3 (L40-44, no trailing {{prompt}}), but it holds a real claim ("The account is a reconstruction, not ground truth") plus an actionable instruction ("Quote a specific file or function back and ask Claude to confirm it read what it claims") — not a bare wait-state bullet.

All 5 headers are literally true of their chunk content: L21 "Read your repo deliberately" -> read-instruction + prompt (L27-29); L31 "Ask what the agent skipped, and why" -> skip-focused bullets + ask-instruction (L33-38); L40 "Read the self-report, then spot-check it" -> reconstruction claim + spot-check instruction (L42-43); L45 "Check how full the window is" -> ceiling claim + /context instruction (L47-51); L55 "The slice the agent didn't load" -> closing claim on the un-loaded slice (L57-58). No contradiction found.

Checked each sub-item by hand across all chunks: no "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlative; no abstraction-noun stacks ("context window" is a defined term, not a stack); no empty-leg verb triplets. One number+retraction candidate, chunk 3 L42 "Assume about 10% of what it says or does is made up. Could be more or less than this heuristic suggests." — covered by the rule's own EXCEPT clause and the maintainer's dated attestation at L84 ("a loosely-held working prior IS the teaching shape"): accept-with-note, no edit owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 4 of 5 body headings are imperative, as an exercise requires: L21 "Read your repo deliberately", L31 "Ask what the agent skipped, and why", L40 "Read the self-report, then spot-check it", L45 "Check how full the window is". The fifth, L55 "The slice the agent didn't load", is a noun phrase naming its subject rather than an imperative or a general-law claim (unlike the rule's own specimens, e.g. "Anything can be reverse-engineered") — it falls under the explicit NOT-violation carve-out for "catalogue entries naming their subject" (cf. "The numbers"), reinforced by the maintainer's own deliberation over this exact header at L64 and L66.

Closest candidate is the closing bullet, chunk 5 L58 "The slice Claude didn't load stays real" restating header L55 — explicitly accept-noted at L66 (Antti 2026-09-10) as the deliberate beat, not doctrine restatement.
